title: Scalar extension of affine Proj with its chart maps
statement:
Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, let $R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism, and let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ be a commutative graded ring with a ring map $R\to A_0$. Form the graded $S$-algebra $S\otimes_R A$, with homogeneous component $S\otimes_R A_n$, where tensor denotes the usual balanced tensor product with multiplication $(s\otimes a)(t\otimes b)=st\otimes ab$. Let $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B_n$ be a commutative graded ring with an $S$-algebra structure whose unit map $S\to B$ has image in $B_0$ and let $\beta:S\otimes_R A\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ be a graded $S$-algebra isomorphism. Put $\psi(a)=\beta(1\otimes a)$. Use affine Proj [def-nagata-affine-proj], its degree-zero structure map followed by the spectrum map [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to obtain $p_A:\operatorname{Proj}(A)\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $p_B:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}S$. There is a canonical morphism $r_\psi:\operatorname{Proj}(B)\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ making the square with $p_A,p_B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(R\to S)$ cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every homogeneous $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, its inverse image of $D_+(f)$ is $D_+(\psi(f))$ and its restriction to that open is the spectrum morphism induced by
$$A_{(f),0}\longrightarrow B_{(\psi(f)),0},\qquad a/f^m\longmapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$$
[def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. The opens $D_+(\psi(f))$, as $f$ ranges over all positive-degree homogeneous elements of $A$, cover $\operatorname{Proj}(B)$; these formulas uniquely determine $r_\psi$.

proof.text: Put $C=S\otimes_R A$ and $W_f=D_+(\psi(f))\subseteq\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. Every element of $B_n$ for $n>0$ is a finite sum $\sum_i s_i\psi(a_i)$ with $a_i\in A_n$, since $\beta$ identifies $B_n$ with $S\otimes_R A_n$. Thus the ideal generated by all the $\psi(f)$ equals $B_+$: one inclusion follows from their positive degrees and the other from these finite sums. The homogeneous-generator cover in [def-nagata-affine-proj] gives $\bigcup_f W_f=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. The same cover applied to all positive-degree homogeneous elements of $A$ covers $\operatorname{Proj}(A)$.

For $f\in A_d$, $d>0$, apply [lem-nagata-homogeneous-localization-scalar-extension] and then $\beta$ on homogeneous fractions to get an $S$-algebra isomorphism $e_f:S\otimes_R A_{(f),0}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{(\psi(f)),0}$, sending $s\otimes(a/f^m)$ to $s\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$. The last map is well defined because the localization relation $f^k(f^n a-f^m b)=0$ maps to the identical relation with $\psi(f)$; applying $\beta^{-1}$ gives its inverse. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the standard chart identifications in [def-nagata-affine-proj], $W_f$ is the fibre product of $D_+(f)$ with $\operatorname{Spec}S$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Its projection to $D_+(f)$ is induced by $a/f^m\mapsto\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$. Its other projection is the restriction of $p_B$, since both maps on degree-zero coefficients send $s$ to $s/1$.

Let $f\in A_d$, $g\in A_e$ with $d,e>0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], $D_+(f)\cap D_+(g)$ is the principal open of $g^d/f^e$ in the $f$ chart. The chart map in step 2 sends this element to $\psi(g)^d/\psi(f)^e$, whose principal open is $W_f\cap W_g$ by the same cited statement for $B$. Inverse images under spectrum maps are computed by contraction of prime ideals, so the local projection from $W_f$ has inverse image of $D_+(g)$ exactly $W_f\cap W_g$. On this intersection both local maps factor through $D_+(fg)$. To check their ring maps explicitly, take $a\in A_{m(d+e)}$ and choose $k$ with $dk\geq m$. In the localized $f$ chart the fraction $a/(fg)^m$ is $(a g^{dk-m}/f^{m+ek})/(g^d/f^e)^k$: its numerator has degree $d(m+ek)$, and multiplication of fractions proves the equality. The local map sends this expression to $(\psi(a)\psi(g)^{dk-m}/\psi(f)^{m+ek})/(\psi(g)^d/\psi(f)^e)^k=\psi(a)/(\psi(f)\psi(g))^m$. In the localized $g$ chart choose $\ell$ with $e\ell\geq m$ and write $(a f^{e\ell-m}/g^{m+d\ell})/(f^e/g^d)^\ell$; its numerator has degree $e(m+d\ell)$ and its image is the identical fraction $\psi(a)/(\psi(f)\psi(g))^m$. These equalities use the localization relation, so require no cancellation or nonzerodivisor hypothesis. The overlap identifications and restriction maps are those of [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle]. Equality of these ring maps gives equality of scheme maps by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues the local projections to $r_\psi$. The inverse-image calculation on each $W_f$ proves globally $r_\psi^{-1}(D_+(g))=W_g$.

proof.text: The square commutes on every $W_f$ by the two projections of the affine fibre product in step 2, and hence commutes globally by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. To prove its universal property, let $T$ be any scheme with $u:T\to\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ and $v:T\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ having equal composites to $\operatorname{Spec}R$. Set $T_f=u^{-1}(D_+(f))$, an open cover of $T$. The chart fibre product from step 2 and [def-pc-fibre-product] give a unique $h_f:T_f\to W_f$ projecting to $u|_{T_f}$ and $v|_{T_f}$. On $T_f\cap T_g$ the step-3 inverse-image equality forces both $h_f$ and $h_g$ into $W_f\cap W_g=W_{fg}$. They have the same projections to $D_+(fg)$ and $\operatorname{Spec}S$, so uniqueness for the chart fibre product indexed by $fg$ makes them equal. Glue them using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $h:T\to\operatorname{Proj}(B)$. Any competing lift restricts to $W_f$ on $T_f$ by step 3 and equals $h_f$ by chart uniqueness; gluing uniqueness makes it $h$. This is exactly the universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product], proving the square cartesian.

source.place: Tag 01N2 (lemma-base-change-map-proj), assertion (2), expanded chartwise universal property

proof.text: Finally, a morphism with the asserted inverse images and chart formulas restricts on every $W_f$ to the spectrum map from step 2, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since the $W_f$ cover by step 1, uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] identifies it with $r_\psi$. Thus the construction is canonical and the specified formulas determine it uniquely.
